name: Question 9
problem:
For the function

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s-5)},\,s>5
$$

find the inverse Laplace transform of $G(s),$ given that
$L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a},\text{ }s>a.$
worked_solution:
Notice that we can write $G(s)$ as 

$$
G(s)=\frac{1}{s(s-5)}=\frac{F(s)}{s},
$$

where $F(s)=\frac{1}{s-5}.$
Also, we know that

$$
L{{e}^{at}}=\frac{1}{s-a}.
$$

Thus, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{F(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-5}} \\  & ={e}^{5t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Additionally, we know that if $L{f(t)}=F(s)$, then

$$
L{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{G(s)} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{F(s)}{s}} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{5τ}\,\text{d}τ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{e}^{5τ}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}({e}^{5t}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

For the function G(s)=1s(s−5),s>5 find the inverse Laplace transform of G(s), given that L{eat}=1s−a, s>a.

a
15(et−1)
b
15(1−e5t)
c
e5t
d
15(e5t−1)
e
1s−5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Notice that we can write G(s) as G(s)=1s(s−5)=F(s)s, where F(s)=1s−5. Also, we know that L{eat}=1s−a. Thus, we get L−1{F(s)}=L−1{1s−5}=e5t.

Additionally, we know that if L{f(t)}=F(s), then L{∫0tf(τ)dτ}=F(s)s.

Using the property above in reverse, we obtain L−1{G(s)}=L−1{F(s)s}=∫0tf(τ)dτ=∫0te5τdτ=15e5τ|0t=15(e5t−1).
